Let $c=\cos\theta$ and solve the resulting quadratic $6c^2-3c-5=0$, rejecting any root outside $[-1,1]$.

walkthrough:
Substitute the double-angle identity $\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1$ into the given equation $3\cos 2\theta = 3\cos\theta + 2$:
$$3(2\cos^2\theta - 1) = 3\cos\theta + 2$$

Collect all terms on the left to form a quadratic equation in $\cos\theta$:
$$6\cos^2\theta - 3\cos\theta - 5 = 0$$

Apply the quadratic formula with $a = 6$, $b = -3$, and $c = -5$:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{-(-3) \pm \sqrt{(-3)^2 - 4(6)(-5)}}{2(6)} = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{9 + 120}}{12} = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{129}}{12}$$

Evaluate both roots using $\sqrt{129} \approx 11.357817$:
First root:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{3 + 11.357817}{12} = \dfrac{14.357817}{12} \approx 1.1965$$
Since $-1 \leq \cos\theta \leq 1$, this root is greater than $1$ and gives no real solutions for $\theta$.
Second root:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{3 - 11.357817}{12} = \dfrac{-8.357817}{12} \approx -0.696485$$

Find the basic reference angle for the valid negative cosine value:
$$\alpha = \arccos(0.696485) \approx 45.854^\circ$$

Determine the angles in the second and third quadrants within the interval $0^\circ \leq \theta \leq 360^\circ$ where cosine is negative:
$$\theta_1 = 180^\circ - 45.854^\circ = 134.146^\circ \approx 134.1^\circ$$
$$\theta_2 = 180^\circ + 45.854^\circ = 225.854^\circ \approx 225.9^\circ$$

State the solutions correct to 1 decimal place:
$$\theta = 134.1^\circ \quad \text{or} \quad \theta = 225.9^\circ$$
